extracted.intended_audience: general news readers and media observers (including journalists and media critics)
extracted.subtask_description: News coverage of a magazine's retraction/handling of a sensitive allegation (Quran desecration) and the ensuing public, political, and institutional reactions; includes implicit standards for journalistic practice and accountability. Useful for assessing media behavior, sourcing, and corrections practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to accepted journalistic standards
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a 'certain journalistic standard that should be met.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted criticism: 'I think there's a certain journalistic standard that should be met. In this instance it was not.' Implies standards include thorough verification, careful sourcing, and editorial oversight; failure invites public and official rebuke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying on a single anonymous source
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not base serious allegations on a single anonymous source that cannot substantiate the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White House: 'This was a report based on a single anonymous source that could not substantiate the allegation that was made.' Pentagon: 'Newsweek hid behind anonymous sources, which by their own admission do not withstand scrutiny.' Anti-pattern: publishing grave allegations (which can have deadly consequences) supported only by one unnamed source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure documentary corroboration and precise sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that the alleged fact appears in the cited report/document and be precise about which document or draft contains the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsweek said its information came from a 'knowledgeable government source' who later said he could not be certain he had seen the account in the military report and that it 'might have been in other investigative documents or drafts.' Guidance: check which report/draft contains the allegation; do not conflate drafts, investigative files, and official reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek and report responses from implicated institutions/officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempt to obtain comment from relevant officials and report their responses (or refusals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reporters 'had sought comment from two Defense Department officials. One declined to respond, and the other challenged another part of the story but did not dispute the Quran charge.' Guidance: document efforts to contact, include denials/confirmations, and note when comment is declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent about source uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose when sources express uncertainty about what they saw or cannot confirm facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsweek later disclosed the source said he 'could not be sure he read about the alleged Quran incident in the report' and that it 'might have been in another document.' Best practice: include such caveats prominently at time of publication rather than after backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue timely and appropriate corrections or retractions
rubrics_metrics.description: When factual errors are identified, correct or retract the story appropriately; partial retractions may be seen as insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White House comment: 'while Newsweek now acknowledges that they got the facts wrong, they refuse to retract the story.' Editor Mark Whitaker expressed regret: 'We regret that we got any part of our story wrong...' Guidance: correction language should match the scope of the error and avoid seeming evasive; full retraction may be required for demonstrably false central claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and address consequences of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and take responsibility for the real-world consequences of reporting, especially when it incites violence or damages reputations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: McClellan: 'The report has had serious consequences. People have lost their lives. The image of the United States abroad has been damaged.' Pentagon: story was 'demonstrably false' and 'had significant consequences that reverberated throughout Muslim communities.' Guidance: factor potential harms into editorial decisions and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apologize and offer sympathies when errors cause harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish an apology and extend sympathies to victims and others affected when reporting contains errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor Mark Whitaker: 'We regret that we got any part of our story wrong, and extend our sympathies to victims of the violence and to the U.S. soldiers caught in its midst.' Guidance: apologies should be clear, specific about what was wrong, and directed to those harmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish verified information from rumor or misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve processes to separate verified facts from rumors or misinformation, especially in contexts where prior abuses make allegations more believable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condoleezza Rice: noted difficulty 'when there is rumor or misinformation' and the need to 'deal better with those circumstances.' Guidance: be especially careful in environments where past abuses (e.g., Abu Ghraib) make unverified allegations more plausible to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to ongoing investigation and official follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue investigating disputed charges and cooperate with or report on official inquiries until facts are established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitaker: 'Top administration officials have promised to continue looking into the charges, and so will we.' Guidance: news organizations should follow up on contested allegations and report substantive findings from official investigations.
